restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224); total work over all processors, including construction of the exact published starting solution (charged at 2^35 = 34,359,738,368 units) and the statically audited 2^32-bucket table build plus the packed stage-16/17 table (at most 675,374,525,842,432 / 2224 < 303,675,596,153 units), both in preprocessing. The published Fig. 6 characteristic is public algorithm text and its historical discovery is not charged (public-characteristic); charging the measured re-derivation (32 x 593,858 CPU-s at 2^23 units = 159,412,543,029,248 units) would give 2^47.2483.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes; complete SHA-256 with standard IV, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits; outputs verified by full recomputation and accompanied by a verified 128-byte 32-step collision certificate.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang, Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080), using its Fig. 6 characteristic as public algorithm text and its starting solution as charged advice; truncation, table and Step-2/3 tests follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), re-implemented and re-measured in #296 (mitchuski), with the certified 32-step witness and deterministic compact-table slice replay from #227 (yudduy). On organizer-generated inputs, the replay checks one witness lineage; bit-exact equivalence and operation counts (Swar7Counter) of its 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR C_32 evaluator against seven scalar evaluations, including the lazy CV1 extraction; and bit-exact equivalence, carry-free lane sums and operation counts (Stage16Counter) of the 7-lane stage-16/17 kernel against scalar stage-16/17 tests, including a full 2^14-row group and the certified pair's row. It does not validate the 32-bit-bucket table cardinalities, completeness, build cost or full-run resource bound.

One run of T = 30,702,253,861,697 independent uniform first-block trials, evaluated in B_7 = ceil(T/7) = 4,386,036,265,957 full 7-lane 36-bit guard-bit SWAR batches at 2,732 primitive operations per batch: 2,238 counted arithmetic/randomness operations (32 input rand+mask, 512 schedule, 1,664 rounds, 16 feed-forward, 14 extraction of CV1[0] per lane, verified by Swar7Counter in replay.py), 398 itemized straight-line traffic (one address operation per load or store) and 96 reserve. Each 36-bit lane has 4 guard bits absorbing modular sums so each lane add is 1 op. Another 32 operations (20 itemized) are charged per used trial for the direct 2^32-bucket lookup and control, under the counted Step-2/3 cap 115.1 T. All unused slots in the final batch are charged; no restarts.

The full product of the declared per-trial lower-bound factors and one-sided Bernstein (excess 1.56 T over E[X] <= 113.54, E[X^2] <= 3.563e12, X <= 399,810,656,288) gives cap-stop probability < 4.983e-5 and success > 0.3901004. Exact integer ceilings total 7,756,629,139,234 units (A+B < 7,418,593,804,713; C <= 303,675,596,153; D = 2^35), log2 = 42.8185669637 < 42.819; preprocessing 338,035,334,521 < 2^38.2984. Base: passed d8d39011 (Meganpark980320, 43.001: full-key TAB2 buckets, re-optimised cap, itemised traffic) on 621d0fb0 (Meganpark980320) = Th0rgal's passed f310d44f (47.275) with the characteristic as public algorithm text. Our changes (proof Section 8.2): seven-lane SWAR stages 16-17, lazy CV1[1..7] extraction, and cap/T re-optimised for them.

This version's Step-3 and per-trial changes: stages 16 and 17 run seven P4 candidates per 256-bit word on ten packed 36-bit-lane streams built in C, computing exactly the base's step-16/17 sums and E16, A16, E17, A17 XOR-conformance tests (48 per W14 group, 40 per packed word, 160 per packed word with a stage-16 pass, 96 per stage-17 pass, then the unchanged 2,048 scalar stages 18..31); CV1[1..7] of a lane are extracted only for a trial whose bucket is nonempty (56 operations inside the capped work).

Conditional-selection premise: V counts accepted TAB2 record occurrences. Conditionally on V >= 1, an analysis-only auxiliary seed sampled independently after the trial chooses J uniformly from those V occurrences. The declared selected-valid-tuple-success-transfer heuristic gives Pr[Step3(J) succeeds | V >= 1] >= 3 * 2^-30 (1 - 2^-20). The counterfactual uncapped trial tests every occurrence, so success through J implies uncapped-trial success; the cap is then handled separately by a union bound.

Heuristic bound: relies on public-characteristic, q-32step-matching-rate, step3-46-conditions, selected-valid-tuple-success-transfer, attack-work-moments, swar-stage1617-kernel, precomputation-op-cap, valid-tuple-pairs and starting-solution-cost (score-critical), plus route-search-measured, cpu-second-pricing (fallback only) and search-peak-memory (supporting).

heuristics.statement: The published signed characteristic of Li, Liu, Wang and Shi (CRYPTO 2026, Fig. 6), as truncated to 32 steps in public hash-smash #26/#33, and its two-bit conditions under the stated readings are public algorithm text that the algorithm may use without charging their original discovery. They are a table of conditions, not a collision, and contain no message word, chaining value or state value.
heuristics.scope: The signed rows and two-bit conditions only. Every value-level object (the starting solution, tables P1-P4, first blocks, valid tuples, second blocks) is computed and charged: D = 2^35, C <= 301,759,726,000 units, and the online work A + B (proof Sections 4, 8).
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication and restated in proof Section 2; the authors' search model is public (Peace9911/sha_2_attack), and #396's completed re-run of S's procedure returned exactly these signed rows. The organizer-accepted SHA-256 r31 package 50592e75 (heuristic H1-public-characteristic) uses the same convention for the published 31-step characteristic. The cost model's omitted-search rule is honoured for every value-level object (proof Section 6.1); the characteristic is stored within the 2^13-byte advice bound.
heuristics.limitations: The historical discovery cost of the characteristic is not charged. If a reviewer charged the measured re-derivation (32 x 593,858 CPU-s at 2^23), the total of this version would be 2^47.2483021516 (f310d44f claimed 2^47.2721673216 with the same E); with no rediscovery factor, 2^43.5343.

heuristics.statement: A uniform first block M0 compressed with C_32 from the IV yields at least 2^-17.3584 expected valid tuple occurrences (accepted TAB2 records in Step 2) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 records.
heuristics.scope: The exact TAB2 and Step-2 tests of proof Section 4 with C_32 first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact-enumeration prediction 2^-17.3254; four measured runs, 2^34 part-trials and 25,936 valid tuples give pooled q_hat = 25,936/2^32 = 2^-17.3373. A one-sided normal approximation to the summed rare-event counts gives the 99% lower bound (25,936 - 2.32635 sqrt(25,936))/2^32 = 2^-17.3583236, rounded downward here to 2^-17.3584. The retained tuple slice replay verifies one fixed derivation but does not estimate q.
heuristics.limitations: Large-scale rate runs are participant C executions; treats CV1 words as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple drawn uniformly from the pooled accepted TAB2 record occurrences of fresh uniform trials (the occurrence-weighted distribution), the declared heuristic premise is that each of its 196,608 (W14,W15) candidates conforms through step 22 and W16..W31 with probability at least 2^-46, and Step 3 succeeds with r >= 3 * 2^-30 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Steps 16..22 and W16..W31 of the second block for the occurrence-weighted valid-tuple distribution; candidates are grouped by W14 (12 groups of 2^14), with that grouping used in the Bonferroni pair correction for r. Transfer to the trial-weighted, analysis-only uniformly selected tuple after conditioning on V >= 1 is separately declared.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured cumulative stage rates through step 21 over 2^32.25 candidates match the condition mapping. The 13 later conditions are extrapolated; the certified 128-byte witness and fixed replay demonstrate feasibility of one full conformance, not its rate.
heuristics.limitations: Independence beyond the W14 grouping is not proved; the 13 W20/W22 carry conditions after step 21 are extrapolated from the condition count. The single certified witness demonstrates feasibility only and supplies no rate evidence. This generic tuple premise alone does not justify conditioning on V >= 1 or selecting a tuple from that trial.

heuristics.statement: For a fresh uniform first-block trial conditioned on V >= 1 accepted TAB2 record occurrences, let an analysis-only auxiliary seed sampled independently after the trial choose J uniformly from those V occurrences. The conditional probability that Step 3 on J contains at least one fully conforming P4 candidate is at least r = 3 * 2^-30 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: The fixed submitted TAB2 and P4, exact Step-2 test and Step-3 test over fresh independent uniform first blocks. J is an analysis-only uniform selector over accepted record occurrences and adds no coins or work to the submitted algorithm. The counterfactual uncapped trial tests every occurrence, so success through J is contained in uncapped-trial success; the cap is handled separately.
heuristics.extrapolation: The condition mapping and pooled participant stage rates through step 21 support the occurrence-weighted valid-tuple model. From E[C(V,2)] <= q/32 and Pr[V>=1] >= 31q/32, at most 1/31 of nonempty trials have V>=2; also E[V 1_{V>=2}] <= 2E[C(V,2)] <= q/16, so at least 15/16 of occurrence mass comes from singleton trials where the two selectors coincide. This is relevance evidence only: the declared transfer still assumes that conditioning on V>=1 and changing to a trial-first, then uniform-within-trial selector do not reduce Step-3 success below r.
heuristics.limitations: No participant campaign reports Step-3 outcomes stratified by V or compares occurrence-weighted with trial-weighted uniform-tuple rates, and no complete late-stage pass occurred in the rate campaign. The pair bound does not exclude concentration of the very rare Step-3 successes in multi-tuple trials; multiplicity and success may be correlated. The certified witness proves feasibility only; if this conditional transfer fails, the 0.39 success claim is unsupported.

heuristics.statement: Fallback only, not in the claimed total: Constructing the published 35-step characteristic, given its nabla W as part of the advice, costs at most 32 times the solver CPU time of the measured run of S's procedure (M_E = 593,858 CPU-seconds); the charged upper bound is exactly 159,412,543,029,248 < 2^47.179759 target-compression units at 2^23 units per CPU-second.
heuristics.scope: Fallback only: the characteristic search, if a reviewer charges it (proof Section 6.2). Not part of the claimed total; its memory is declared under search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: The public PR #396 run executed S's four-step procedure with the authors' model library until a Step-4 call at threshold 76 returned a characteristic equal to Fig. 6 in every signed row; all 59 calls and 593,858 CPU-seconds are charged. The factor 32 is an itemised blind-rediscovery factor of about 8 (priced from its timed-out blind descent and three tA levels) times a residual factor 4 (solver variance and exploratory-model/nabla-W choice).
heuristics.limitations: Steps 2-4 were conditioned on S's nabla W, and Step 4 targeted S's published thresholds rather than completing a blind descent; 76 was reached but not proved optimal. The x32 margin prices blind rediscovery from the run ledger but was not itself executed, and S's historical time is unpublished. Enters only the fallback total 2^47.2721673216 for a reviewer who charges the characteristic search (proof Section 6.2).

heuristics.statement: Fallback only, not in the claimed total: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most 2^23 target-compression units (2^34.12 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations, 17.0 operations per retired instruction).
heuristics.scope: Fallback only: the measured STP+CryptoMiniSat characteristic-search run and its x32 allowance (proof Section 6.2).
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured 2^30.03 instructions per CPU-second (callgrind count of a deterministic call against native CPU time) and opcode mix (multiply/divide/floating point 0.42%, unmapped 7.24%) leave 17.0 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations per instruction at kappa = 2^23 (as in #134), with full sensitivity at 2^24 and 2^25 reported in Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: One single-thread calibration instance; instruction rate under the run's machine load. Enters only the fallback total 2^47.2721673216 for a reviewer who charges the characteristic search (proof Section 6.2).

heuristics.statement: E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5 for the number V of valid tuples in one trial.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples sharing one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials; cross-part term estimated from multiplicity sums with the observed correlation factor; charge exceeds the estimate by more than 20x.

heuristics.statement: The fixed submitted TAB2 has maximum bucket occupancy at most 936 (27-bit buckets, hence also its 32-bit-bucket refinement). For the counterfactual uncapped counted Step-2/3 work demand X of one independent uniform first-block trial under the 2^32-bucket scan, the lazy CV1[1..7] extraction, the seven-lane stage-16/17 kernel and the stage-17 early abort, E[X] <= 113.54, E[X^2] <= 3.563e12 and 0 <= X <= 399,810,656,288; one-sided Bernstein bounds the probability that the total exceeds 115.1 T by less than 4.983e-5.
heuristics.scope: The Step-2/3 work counter in proof Section 8 and its hard cap W_cap = 115.1 T for T = 30,702,253,861,697 independent uniform first-block trials; the lazy extraction is charged once per nonempty-bucket trial; every packed word of a valid tuple pays the stage-16 word charge, a packed word with a stage-16 pass pays the stage-17 word charge, and candidates that fail stage 17 stop before later work.
heuristics.extrapolation: The inherited full-table participant enumeration reports exact maximum bucket occupancy 936, and the fixed builder asserts that bound before prefix construction. The mean combines the 2^32-bucket mean occupancy N/2^32 < 0.32522 (for a uniform key; also bounds the nonempty-bucket probability), exact table-cardinality rate, Step-2 pass fractions, q upper confidence bound, f16 <= 0.126 and f17 <= 2^-14.9: E[X] <= 5(0.32522) + 56(0.32522) + 0.32522(192) + q_UCB(300 + 12(48 + 2,341*40) + 196,608(160 f16 + 2,144 f17)) < 113.5358. The number of packed words reaching the stage-17 tranche is at most the number of stage-16 passes (union bound, no lane independence assumed). Charged tranches 48, 40, 160, 96 and 2,048 have slack above audited subtotals 30, 26, 138, 61 and 1,866; the lazy extraction 56 above 45. The second moment 3(1.133e6 + 9.119e6 + 1.18759e12) < 3.5629e12 is rounded upward to 3.563e12. The asserted occupancy yields deterministic support X <= 5*936 + 56 + 936*(1304 + 427,146,828) = 399,810,656,288; one-sided Bernstein at excess 1.56 T gives exp(-9.90704798) < 4.983e-5, subtracted in full from the success bound.
heuristics.limitations: The rates, moments and maximum occupancy are participant measurements rather than organizer full-table executions; the bound assumes the claimed random first-block trials transfer those distributions independently and inherits the unobserved cross-part tuple-pair premise. If the fixed table has a bucket above 936, the builder aborts and the success claim fails rather than using the Bernstein bound.

heuristics.statement: The seven-lane kernel (proof Section 4, item 3) passes to stage 18 exactly the P4 candidates that pass the base's scalar stage-16 tests (E16' = E16 xor FL(E16), A16' = A16 xor FL(A16)) and stage-17 tests (E17' = E17 xor FL(E17), A17' = A17 xor FL(A17)), hands stage 18 their exact step-16/17 values, never passes a zero padding lane, and costs at most 48 primitive operations per W14 group, 40 per packed word, 160 per packed word with a stage-16 pass and 96 per stage-17 pass. The lazy extraction returns each trial's exact CV1 at 14 batch extraction operations per seven trials plus 56 per nonempty-bucket trial.
heuristics.scope: Stages 16 and 17 of Step 3 for every valid tuple: 12 W14 groups of 2^14 P4 rows, 2,341 packed words per group (the last with three zero padding lanes), ten packed streams, seven 36-bit lanes per 256-bit word with W16 and c17 broadcast per group; and the CV1 extraction of the 7-trial first-block batch. Stages 18..31, the test order and the stage fractions f16 and f17 are unchanged.
heuristics.extrapolation: Deterministic lane argument (proof Section 8 B): packed streams and broadcast constants are below 2^32 per lane with zero guard bits; step-16 sums are masked to 32 bits before Sigma1, IF, Sigma0 and MAJ; E17 lanes are sums of four and A17 lanes of seven values below 2^32, so every lane stays below 2^35 and no carry crosses a lane; after masking, u_l + 2^32 - 1 sets guard bit 32 iff u_l != 0; padding lanes give E16 xor E16' = 0 != FL(E16) = 0x02808000. The organizer replay (experiment fixed-witness-derivation) compares pass-mask words for both stages and all extracted values bit-for-bit with scalar stage-16/17 tests on organizer-seeded rows (random rows, rows built to pass one or both stages, single-bit near misses at each stage including stage-16 failures whose stage-17 equations hold, carry stress at W16 = 2^32 - 1 and near-maximal lanes), on one full 2^14-row group and on the certified pair's row built from the literal step equations; it asserts every lane addition is carry-free and below 2^35, checks the lazy extraction against scalar C_32, and asserts the counted data-path operations (Stage16Counter: 14 per group, 4 loads + 13 per word, 6 loads + 116 per word with a stage-16 pass, 7 per word with a stage-17 pass, 16 per stage-17 pass; Swar7Counter: 14 + 14 per lane for the extraction). The charges cover itemised subtotals 30, 26, 138, 61 and 45.
heuristics.limitations: The replay is a finite functional check; universality rests on the lane-bound argument in the proof. The traffic/control part of each charge is a static word-RAM ledger in the convention of d8d39011 (one address operation per memory access), not a native instruction count or timing. Lane packing inside Step 3 is new to this line of packages; it relies on the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 exactly as the inherited first-block batch does.

heuristics.statement: The finite no-sort P1-P4 reference pseudocode, with TAB2 bucketed by all 32 bits of A[-1] and the PC-6 packing pass of the stage-16/17 streams, requires at most 675,374,525,842,432 primitive word operations, equal to 303,675,596,152.1727 < 303,675,596,153 < 2^38.143741 target-compression units; the integer ceiling is charged.
heuristics.scope: The one-time 32-bit-bucket TAB2, P4 and packed stage-16/17 table construction charged as term C in proof Section 8, including both W7 passes, record actions, fixed-array administration, bucket zeroing/prefix/cursor checks, auxiliary rows and 280,920 packed words.
heuristics.extrapolation: Static worst-case source audit: the exact PC-1 L4, PC-1 L7, PC-2, PC-3, two-pass PC-4 and PC-5 loop counts are charged their displayed per-iteration maxima 2,096, 3,312, 7,280, 3,760, 3,872 and 6,256, respectively, totaling 665,773,944,631,296 main-loop operations. PC-4 charges its two-sigma0 cancellation equality as a full 128-operation equation body, not a 16-operation predicate. Every W7 candidate in one complete pass receives a separate 64-operation record-action charge; each of the 2^32+1 bucket boundaries (2^27+1 in the audited layout plus 2^32-2^27 added by d8d39011) receives 1,024 operations covering both count/cursor and offset arrays, including the maximum-occupancy assertion; every retained auxiliary row receives another 1,024 operations; and each of the 280,920 PC-6 packed words (12 groups x 2,341 words x 10 streams) receives 1,024 operations. The exact integer sum is divided by C=2224 and rounded upward by less than one target-compression unit to 303,675,596,153.
heuristics.limitations: The exact table cardinalities are inherited participant enumerations from #26/#296. The audit is for the displayed prospective fixed-capacity, no-sort word-RAM pseudocode; it is not a compilable historical source file, native instruction trace, wall-time measurement or organizer full build. Different predicates, capacities, dynamic growth or sorting invalidate the bound.

heuristics.statement: The fixed starting solution used by this algorithm is the single Step-1 solution used by S to build its TAB2 and published collision pair; S reports about 2^34.3 for finding that solution, and the submitted D = 2^35 = 34,359,738,368 target-compression units covers construction of this exact fixed advice.
heuristics.scope: Construction of the exact fixed values A4..A13, E8..E13, W12 and W13 used by P1-P4/TAB2 and the inherited cardinality, rate and work measurements; no substitution of another SAT output.
heuristics.extrapolation: S Sect. 4 first finds one valid through-step-13 solution, fixes the listed state/message words based on it, builds TAB2 and reports about 2^34.3 for finding the Step-1 solution. If that unstated unit is a full 35-step compression, conversion by 2476/2224 gives ceil(2^34.3 x 2476/2224) = 23,547,494,749 < 2^35, leaving a factor 1.459. The two local 908.8-CPU-second alternate-solution runs corroborate task scale only and are not used for transfer.
heuristics.limitations: The historical Step-1 execution was not independently reproduced and S reports only about 2^34.3 without stating its unit or providing a trace. The 1.459 conversion margin therefore remains heuristic. The locally generated solutions differ from T and do not establish interchangeability; the scored algorithm uses only T.

heuristics.statement: The characteristic and starting-solution searches need at most 2^33 bytes at peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory of the characteristic and starting-solution searches, which run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured peak resident set 5.25 GiB over all 59 characteristic-search calls and the two corroborative starting-solution runs; S's historical starting-solution run is assumed not to exceed the same 2^33-byte envelope.
heuristics.limitations: S's historical peak is not reported; the measured peaks are added to the memory bound anyway.
